title: Case
description:
One test: how to invoke the subject, how its dependencies must respond, and what the
result must contain.

allow_fail.description:
A known failure that must not fail the whole suite. Opt in deliberately; it is
never inherited by omission.

fake.description: How the faked dependencies must respond. Omit it when the subject calls nothing.

name.description:
Human-readable name. Also the identifier in reports, so make it say what the case
proves rather than what it does.

setup.description: How to prepare and invoke the subject.

weight.description:
How much this case matters. Reports sort failures by it, and gating thresholds
weigh it.

calls.description:
How many times each faked binary must have been called. A count of `0` asserts a
dependency was **not** touched, which is often the interesting half.

event_counts.description:
How many events of each type must have been emitted. A count of `0` proves one never
happened.

events.description:
Structured events that must appear, in order.

Matched as a **subsequence**: other events may occur in between, and each entry only
constrains the fields it names. An exact list would break the day the subject gains one
new event.

exit_code.description: The exit code the subject must return.

files.description:
Assertions on the files the subject wrote, by path.

A path may use the variables isolation defines — `$HOME`, `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}` and the
rest — or a leading `~`. Anything else is refused rather than left literal, because a
stray `$TYPO` would make an `absent` assertion trivially true.

invariants.description:
Named invariants that must hold. The names come from the project configuration, so a
name nothing declares is a case failure rather than a silent skip.

Match.description:
Criterion selecting a rule. Every field is optional; a `Match` whose fields are
all absent is the **catch-all**.

Deliberately without `deny_unknown_fields`: a project composes its own criterion
on top of this one —
`struct MyMatch { #[serde(flatten)] core: Match, agent: Option<String> }` — and
`flatten` is incompatible with rejecting unknown fields. Catching typos is the
core's job, at case load time, against the JSON schema.

args_contain.description: Substring searched for in the arguments joined by spaces.

bin.description: Name of the faked binary, as the caller spelled it.

call.description: Rank of the call, 1-indexed, for the counter key in force.

stdin_contains.description: Substring searched for in standard input.

Rule.description:
One rule: a criterion and the response that goes with it.

Deliberately not generic over the criterion. A project needing its own criterion
declares its own `Rule` — it has its own response fields anyway — and reuses only
[`Match`] from this crate, flattened under its own. Making `Rule` generic would
mean carrying serde and schemars bounds on the parameter for a benefit nobody is
asking for.

exec.description:
`real` passes through to the real binary, found further along `PATH`. Any
other value is the path of a project executable to delegate to, with the same
arguments.

exit.description: Exit code of the fake. Absent means `0`.

latency_ms.description:
Wait before responding, in milliseconds. Meant to reproduce a
timing-sensitive sequence, not to slow things down for its own sake.

match.description: The criterion deciding whether this rule applies.

stderr.description: What the fake writes on its standard error.

stdout.description: What the fake writes on its standard output.

Scenario.description: The whole scenario, as it reaches the fake binary.

render.description:
Executable that dresses the selected response. It receives the rule and the
call as JSON on its standard input, and returns the bytes to emit.

rules.description: The rules, in the order they are tried.

Setup.description:
How to prepare and invoke the subject.

The core understands exactly two keys, `run` and `exec`. **Everything else is
opaque** and travels untouched into the setup hook, which is what lets a project
write its own vocabulary here without the core learning any domain words.

exec.description:
A project executable that prepares the isolated directory. It receives this whole
block as JSON on its standard input.

run.description:
The command line to invoke, argument by argument. No shell is involved, so there
are no quoting rules to remember.

TextExpectation.description: Assertions on a stream of text.

absent.description:
Substrings that must appear nowhere. This is the family that catches an
unresolved variable or a leaked secret.
